readerQuestion: How can I put a Home Assistant routine button and a room-temperature reading on my Android or iPhone home screen, and tell a failed command from an outdated display?
directAnswer: Use the official Companion app's Android Action button or iPhone Scripts widget to run one saved script, then add a separate temperature display. First verify a helper-only script inside Home Assistant and from the phone. Widget readings can lag; remote control needs a working remote connection, and selected widget entities do not establish account-level restrictions.
originalContribution: Sections 1-4 supply one shared, harmless Toggle-helper script, exact editor placement, platform-specific button setup, and a four-case verification table. An explicit turn_on command makes repeated taps predictable. Section 5 separates script failure, server connectivity, navigation instead of execution, stale display, and mobile-data access, with a small next check for each.
limitations: Documentation research and automated editorial/browser review, not a human or expert review or hands-on phone/device test. YAML was parsed and its single helper-on action checked locally, but not executed on a Home Assistant instance. Installed app/OS versions can differ; the documented iOS Custom Widget remains BETA and background refresh is not guaranteed. Cover is disclosed generated editorial art, not a screenshot or installation photograph.
proofreadFixes: Made the Android Data Saver step actionable rather than saying only to check the setting. Added a navigation-versus-script troubleshooting row and a harmless reproduction path for unresolved app-version issues. Clarified that a widget refresh timestamp does not establish a fresh sensor measurement, and that the helper, not the short-lived script state, is the persistent test result. Kept explicit on rather than toggle, no physical action in the first rehearsal, optional lamp testing separate, and paid Cloud access labeled at the recommendation. Confirmed four direct TLDR bullets, visible linked Tara Home credit, honest research method, and professional source labels. Final read and desktop/mobile checks found no remaining publication-blocking issue.

claimChecks.claim: Android provides an Action button and Entity State widget. A green check confirms an action call, not a physical outcome; Data Saver and background-data settings affect widgets. Faster refresh may require additional permissions and settings differ by Android version.

iOS supports Scripts and Sensors widgets; the approximately 15-minute sensor interval is not a real-time guarantee. Custom Widget is documented as BETA, offers explicit Run script behavior and a last-update display, and remains subject to OS refresh budgets.
Apple documents the Home Screen Edit, Add Widget and edit-widget procedure used to place the iPhone widget.
A Toggle helper stores software on/off state. input_boolean.turn_on sets it on rather than toggling it; the initial test targets only a new helper kept out of existing automations.

A saved script supplies a reusable sequence with single mode. The example belongs in one script editor and needs no parameters; its helper records the outcome independently of whether the script is still running.

light.turn_on and light.toggle are distinct actions. The optional physical follow-up uses an already working nonessential light and a separate script; no lock, alarm or garage-door action is used for verification.

Away-from-home operation needs remote connectivity. Home Assistant Cloud is a subscription option; VPN access requires a configured and connected private route. A widget does not provide remote access by itself.
Home Assistant treats logged-in users as trusted. A limited widget selection, non-admin account or confirmation prompt does not establish room-only entity authorization.
Dashboard view visibility hides tabs while the URL remains accessible; hidden views are not presented as a server-enforced access boundary.
